facts.text: On this date in 1095, Pope Urban II launched the First Crusade at Clermont, France — setting in motion a series of wars that would reshape three continents and define the next four centuries of geopolitics.

On this date in 1942, the French navy scuttled 77 warships in Toulon harbor to prevent Nazi seizure — the largest deliberate destruction of a naval fleet in history, sunk by its own sailors in under three hours.
Mongolia has more horses than people. Its 3.5 million residents share the country with roughly 4.3 million horses, many still used daily for herding across a landmass twice the size of Texas.

Jakarta is sinking up to 25 centimeters per year in some districts — faster than sea level is rising — which is why Indonesia has already moved its capital to a new city, Nusantara, carved from Borneo jungle.

The entire population of Australia could fit inside the city limits of London with room to spare. Australia's 27 million people occupy the world's sixth-largest country; London's footprint holds 35 million at similar density.
On this date in 1895, Alfred Nobel signed his will establishing the Nobel Prizes — funded entirely by his fortune from dynamite patents, worth roughly $250 million in today's money.
On Nov 27, 2013, the Dow closed above 16,000 for the first time. It had taken 14 years to double from 8,000.
The S&P 500 has a longer losing streak record for Mondays than any other weekday — markets statistically dread the start of the week more than the end.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A shares have never split. At over $700,000 per share, buying a single one costs more than most Americans earn in a decade.
The tulip bulb at the peak of Tulipmania in 1637 cost roughly ten times a skilled craftsman's annual salary — for a flower that would rot within a year.
On this date in 1783, John Michell described a star so massive light couldn't escape it — 216 years before we photographed one. He called them 'dark stars.' We call them black holes.
Your bone marrow produces 2.4 million red blood cells every second. By the time you finish this sentence, you've made roughly 10 million.
On this date in 1895, Alfred Nobel signed his will establishing the prizes — motivated, historians believe, by a premature obituary calling him a 'merchant of death.'
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh 10 million tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon in complete darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit of light sensitivity.
On this day in 1095, Pope Urban II launched the First Crusade. That speech is older than the Aztec Empire, Oxford University, and the existence of the word 'Europe' as a common term.
Jimi Hendrix and Mozart died at the same age — 27 — separated by 178 years. Mozart just had better PR for longer.
On this day in 1942, Casablanca premiered in New York — rushed out to capitalize on the Allied invasion of North Africa that had happened just weeks earlier. The film was current events.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, before the American Civil War. For most of its existence, it sat useless — waiting 140 years for offices to care.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, when Grover Cleveland was U.S. president and the Eiffel Tower was brand new. It spent its first 85 years selling playing cards.

Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of a used bookshop. Coined by John Koenig in *The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows* (2013), it has no older root — sometimes a word is simply needed into existence.

Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to, or one that never existed. It folds grief, nostalgia, and belonging into a single syllable cluster English has never managed to replicate.

On this day in 1095, Pope Urban II concluded the Council of Clermont — the speech that launched the First Crusade. The Latin word *peregrinus*, pilgrim, shares its root with *peregrine*: both mean 'one who travels through foreign lands.'

On this day in 1942, Casablanca's real-world namesake film began its Hollywood premiere run. The word *casablanca* is simply Spanish for 'white house' — the same words, in the same order, that name the American presidency's residence.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego describing the shared glance between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists cite it as one of the most meaning-dense single words ever documented.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's price crossed $10,000 for the first time — but the more remarkable fact is that miners that day earned more in fees alone than the entire network's block reward just two years prior.
On this date in 2022, the FTX bankruptcy estate listed among its assets a $7.3M purchase of naming rights to a Miami arena that had already been renamed back to FTX Arena for under two weeks.
Ethereum's gas limit is not set by the protocol — it's a soft consensus among miners and validators who vote each block to adjust it up or down by 0.1%, making it emergent rather than constitutional.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — but it also pays no coinbase reward to any spendable address, making Satoshi's first 50 BTC permanently unspendable by design.

Uniswap v2 introduced a 0.05% protocol fee that was deliberately left switched off at launch — the governance switch to activate it has never been flipped, leaving billions in cumulative fees uncollected by the protocol treasury.

On this date in 2022, ChatGPT launched publicly. It reached 1 million users in 5 days — faster than any consumer product in history — and forced every major tech company to emergency-restructure its roadmap within 90 days.

On this date in 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need.' The transformer architecture it introduced now underlies virtually every large language model in production, yet the paper was initially rejected from one workshop.

AlphaFold 2 predicted the 3D structure of nearly every known protein — roughly 200 million — in under a year. The same task had occupied structural biologists for five decades and would have taken millennia by experimental methods alone.

GPT-4 was trained on an estimated ~2×10²⁵ FLOPs. For context, that exceeds the total number of seconds since the Big Bang by seven orders of magnitude, executed in a matter of months on purpose-built silicon.

The first neural network to defeat a human Go champion, AlphaGo in 2016, was itself beaten by AlphaGo Zero 18 months later — a system that learned purely from self-play, never having seen a single human game.
